input.quote: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
input.rationale: The Term runs eight years (p0049). Customer's convenience right in 11.1 exists but requires a full year's notice and payment of a redacted percentage of Estimated Remaining Value plus unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses (treated as liquidated damages under 13.5), which fails the fallback (60–90 days' notice; fee capped at three months' fees). On the Vendor side, Section 10.2 lets M&I withdraw any non-Core Services "at any time" on 90 days' notice — a mid-term convenience exit, whereas the fallback permits Vendor convenience termination only at the end of a term (the 90-day notice requirement is already satisfied). We therefore target the fallback rather than preferred, because stripping the fee entirely would require collateral rewrites of 11.2(A) and 13.5: we cut our notice to 90 days, cap all Section 11.1 early-termination amounts at three months' fees, and tie M&I's withdrawal right to the end of the Term.

proposal.summary: Cut Customer's convenience notice to 90 days and cap all early-termination amounts at three months' fees; limit M&I's withdrawal of Services to the end of the Term.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We reduced our convenience-termination notice from one year to ninety (90) days and capped the Termination for Convenience Fee (together with the other amounts charged under Section 11.1) at three months' fees, which is our fallback position. We also required that M&I's withdrawal of Services take effect only at the end of the Term, since M&I should not have a mid-term convenience exit.
